snippets.text: All right, it's time for a class guide.
Global is around the corner or depending
on when you watch this, it might already
be here. In this guide, I'm going to try
and help give you some insight as to how
the cleric class plays out and its build
priority. With that being said, it's
important to note that as time goes on
with patches and balance changes, things
will be subject to change. As you
probably already assumed, the cleric
class is the dedicated support class.
You are the healer and res bot, but
that's not all. I played the Taiwan
launch for about 6 to 8 months and
cleared all the PvE content that the
game had to offer. I also grinded out
Supreme Commander in the Abyss and while
grinding an unhealthy amount of hours
into this game, I learned that the
cleric's priority most of the time is to
make sure every debuff you have to offer
is up on the target 100% of the time so
your DPS can go crazy. It's not quite
like other MMOs where you can just heal
and hang back. You're kind of a DPS
class where healing is secondary. And
before you argue with me about this,
just understand that I'm not saying it's
not your responsibility to cleanse and
heal because it still is and both
cleansing and healing are obviously
still important. What I'm saying is that
as you run through content, you'll
notice that a lot of the important
mechanics can't always be healed through
anyway. So basically, if someone messes
up a minor mechanic, you can cleanse or
heal to reset them, but when that big
mechanic comes around, if they mess it
up, that's GG for them and then you
either res or they use a res stone. So
when you're in a group that knows the
content, you end up just debuffing and
DPSing 90% of the time. And I know this
game is just launching now so there'll
be a lot of new people coming in that
don't know the mechanics. So you'll
likely have to do more healing than
necessary, but debuffing the boss should
still be a priority. Okay, so now that
that's out of the way, what stigmas
might you want to use? Here it's
important to note that for season 1 of
global, you'll only be able to equip
four stigma skills at a time. Whereas on
Taiwan, you can currently have six. So
when looking at any builds from Taiwan,
you'll need to make some adjustments. So
for now, we're just working with four
stigmas for PvE. All of the stigmas get
better as you level them, but looking at
what I can expect to get from them
immediately, the four I'm probably going
to choose will be light of protection as
it offers both PvE damage and tolerance
for you and your party members at its
base level, resurrection for obvious
reasons, Earth's Punishment. This one
synergizes well with condemnation, which
will end up being your main source of
damage. Looking at condemnation, you see
it will reset on landing a critical hit,
and Earth's Punishment level five
guarantees that condemnation will crit.
So, you'll be able to really pump while
this is up. And for the fourth, Noble
Aura as it will provide constant damage.
This one you can swap with Prayer of
Amplification possibly if you want. I'm
sure it'll work too. I'll have to test
it out on launch to see which provides
more damage over the course of a fight.
Or if you're finding that you need to do
a lot of healing, you can swap it out
for Absolution or Benevolence. So, now
that we have our stigmas, what would our
skill priority look like? Going back to
what I said earlier about our priority
being to keep the target debuffed, you
can see I've stacked my debuff abilities
onto my right click so I can ensure that
they are up 100% of the time. We have
Debilitating Mark, which reduces the
target's damage boost and defense,
Chains of Torment reducing their damage
tolerance, then Earth's Punishment,
which will give our condemnation more
crit as well as give you and your party
members more double attack, defense, and
grant more damage as you level up. Once
all of these are out, you're basically
just spamming your auto attack with left
click or weaving your auto attack with
Judgment with left click if you have it
set to an in-game macro. Currently on
Taiwan, it's more single target damage
to just auto attack and not use
Judgment, but we'll have to see what
happens on global with this. While
holding left click, you're also mashing
or holding your right click to spam out
your condemnation resets as well as
reapply your debuffs when they come up.
Of course, you're keeping your other
abilities on cooldown as well as healing
and cleansing when needed. But with this
setup, it's basically just holding left
and right click for the most part. When
it comes to your healing abilities,
ideally you'll want to try and get them
all leveled up as quick as possible in
order to strengthen them and unlock all
the customizations. But, what I would
recommend is to try and get healing
light to level 16 as soon as possible,
so you have something you can spam if
things get hairy. Also, run cleanse on
your radiant recovery and movement speed
on your light of regen. Your party
members will thank you. There is going
to be people that use third-party
programs and set up macros through that,
and I can't help you with that. This
setup here is only using what's provided
to me through the game. Next are
passives. There's really only three I'd
pay any attention to for PvE, starting
with Empyrean Lord's Grace, as it
increases your crit and also deals extra
damage when landing attacks every 1
second. Second is Earth's Grace for more
crit damage boost, and third being
healing enhancement. This helps
strengthen your heals by increasing the
amount it scales off of your attack. As
for your stat priority, there's not much
unique here. Just get as much attack,
crit, and double as you can, while
maintaining the minimum amount of
accuracy for each tier of content, while
also trying to get your hands on as much
illusion as possible for the cooldown
reduction. As for the arcanas, there's
no real need for the two-set magic bonus
here, because you don't really have mana
problems if you're not weaving in
judgment. So, you can go for the vigor
four-set bonus. I'd recommend going with
the Chalice of Vigor, as it will give
you time for combat speed. The parchment
will give you life for more HP. The
compass will give you freedom for more
accuracy. And the mirror for illusion to
get more cooldown reduction. The only
one you'd really want from the magic set
would be the bell, because it gives
destruction for more attack. If you find
that you have too much accuracy, you
could consider switching over your
compass for some extra crit from death,
but you'd be giving up the four-set.
Same goes for the mirror if you'd rather
the double from wisdom. When it comes to
PvP, I'll probably drop a PvP specific
guide shortly after launch. That's
pretty much it for this one. I hope this
has helped. If you have any questions,
feel free to leave them below in my
Discord or swing by the stream. See you
next time.
